Hello 2020, and a new year of learning and growth for all of us! As we begin this new year, I thought I would share with you a few of my favorite resources for learning about the world of data science and machine learning. These resources are a great way to start building a foundation in data science and machine learning, and to stay up to date with the latest developments in the field.
First up, I would like to recommend the Coursera course by Andrew Ng on Machine Learning. This course is a great way to get started with machine learning and covers a wide range of topics, including linear regression, logistic regression, and neural networks. The course is taught by the same professor who taught the highly successful Coursera course on Artificial Intelligence, and is taught in a way that is accessible to anyone with a basic understanding of mathematics and statistics.
Next, I would like to recommend the book "Hands-On Machine Learning with Python" by Aurélien Géron. This book is a great way to learn about machine learning and to gain practical experience with Python programming. It covers a wide range of topics, including data preprocessing, feature engineering, and model selection, and provides a hands-on approach to learning.
Another great resource for learning about data science and machine learning is the Kaggle platform. Kaggle is a community of data scientists and machine learning experts, and provides a wide range of datasets and competitions for data science enthusiasts to work on. Kaggle also has a great blog where you can find articles and tutorials on a wide range of topics related to data science and machine learning.
Finally, I would like to recommend the book "Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning" by Christopher Bishop, et al. This book is a great way to learn about the theoretical foundations of machine learning and provides a comprehensive overview of the most important concepts and techniques in the field.
I hope these resources are helpful for you as you begin your journey into the world of data science and machine learning. Happy learning!
